greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. We gather today in the presence of the Living God, who knows our hearts and calls us to walk in the light of His love.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you are the Way, the Truth, and the Life. Lord, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you are the light that shines in the darkness. Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you are the love that never fails. Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Blessed the people the Lord has chosen to be his own.
homily:
We often think of love as a feeling—a warm, soft emotion that rises when things are easy, when the table is set, when the day is bright. We think of it as a response to kindness, or a reward for goodness. But St. Paul, in his letter to the Corinthians, strips away our comfortable definitions. He tells us that love is not a feeling at all; it is a way of being. It is a way of seeing. He says, 'Love is patient, love is kind... it does not seek its own interests, it is not quick-tempered.' He describes a love that is steady, a love that persists when the world is chaotic, a love that 'bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.'

Think of the image Paul gives us of the mirror. 'At present we see indistinctly, as in a mirror, but then face to face.' We live in the 'indistinct' time. We look at our lives, at the empty spaces in our homes, at the questions that keep us awake, and we see only a reflection. We see the partial. We see the fragments. We see the boy who loved airplanes and dreamed of 'con chim airlines,' the boy whose curiosity was a bright, living fire, the boy whose smile could fill a room. And because we are human, we want to see the whole picture. We want to know why the pieces shifted. We want to know why the melody changed. But Paul reminds us that we know only partially. We are not yet in the room where the light is perfect. We are still standing before the mirror.

I want to talk to you about the 'mirror' of your own hearts, Alan and Thao. I know that for the last three months, you have been looking into that mirror, trying to find the face of your son, Benjamin. You look for him in the morning when the house is quiet. You look for him in the dreams that visit you, like the one where he was waiting in line for ice cream, or the one where he stood tall and strong at the door. You look for him in the laughter of his brother, Ryan. And sometimes, the reflection in the mirror feels like a ghost, a reminder of what is absent. But the Gospel today challenges us to change our perspective. Jesus speaks to the crowds, saying, 'We played the flute for you, but you did not dance. We sang a dirge, but you did not weep.' He is telling us that we often miss the reality of God because we are too busy waiting for the world to play the music we expect.

We expect the music of a long life. We expect the music of a future that unfolds exactly as we planned—the graduation, the career, the milestones, the growing old together. When the song changes, when the dirge begins to play, we struggle to hear the voice of God in the new melody. We think that if the music isn't what we wanted, God must be silent. But God is not silent. He is simply playing a different song. He is playing the song of the eternal. And that song, the song of love, is the only one that never fails. 'Love never fails,' Paul says. It does not cease when the breath stops. It does not fade when the years pass. It simply changes the way it moves through the world.

Benjamin’s love is not a memory. It is a presence. It is a force that continues to move through you, his parents, and through you, Ryan. Think of the way he looked at the world—with that brilliant, curious, tender gaze. He was a boy who understood that to live is to give. Remember how he wanted to offer his piggy bank to help his uncle? He didn't need to empty it. He didn't need to break it. The offer itself was the act of love. That is the 'excellent way' Paul speaks of. That is the way of the heart that is already living in the light of the eternal. Benjamin was already practicing the language of heaven, the language of total, selfless giving.

Alan and Thao, I know the weight you carry. I know the nights when the silence feels like a physical presence, a weight that presses down on your chest. You might feel as though you are failing because you are still grieving, because you are still weeping, because you are still looking for him in the mirror of your daily life. But hear this: grief is not a lack of faith. Grief is the shape that love takes when it can no longer find its object in the physical world. It is the way your heart continues to hold him. You are not failing. You are loving. And that love is the very thing that binds you to him still.

Ryan, my dear brother, you know this better than anyone. You and Ben were a team. You shared the adventures, the travel, the quiet moments in the pews, the dreams of the future. You are the one who carries his story forward. When you feel the quiet, remember that your brother is not a ghost. He is a child of the light. He is at the Banquet. He is seeing the face of the One he loved, and he is cheering for you with that same bright, gentle smile. He is watching over you. He is part of you. You are a brother, and that is a bond that death cannot touch. It is a bond that is being held in the heart of God.

There is a deep peace that comes when we stop trying to force the world to play our music and start listening for God’s. The world says that when a life ends, the story is over. The world says that the ledger is closed. But the Gospel of Jesus Christ says that the story is only beginning. 'Wisdom is vindicated by all her children.' Benjamin is one of those children. He is a child of wisdom, a child of light, a child who has already put aside 'childish things' and is now seeing the face of the Father. He is the one who is now teaching you how to love from the other side of the mirror.

I want to speak to those of you who might be carrying a heavy stone of self-reproach. Maybe you find yourself replaying the past, wondering if you missed a sign, or if you could have done more. Please, hear this truth today: God does not send these sorrows as a punishment, and He does not hold you responsible for the mysteries of life that are beyond human control. You were the parents Benjamin needed. You were the family he loved. You did not miss anything. You are not being accused by God, and you must not accuse yourselves. Let that stone fall. You are free to grieve, you are free to miss him, but you are not required to carry the weight of 'what if.' That is a burden that Christ has already taken upon Himself. He is the one who holds Benjamin in His arms, and who holds you in His heart.

There is a beauty in the way you have honored him. The 'Well of Love' in Vietnam, the way his kindness continues to flow into the lives of those who have never met him—this is his life, still being lived. This is the 'excellent way' in action. You are not just remembering a boy; you are continuing his work. You are making sure that his curiosity, his kindness, and his gentle, brilliant spirit continue to touch the world. That is how you live for him. That is how you keep the bond alive.

What do you carry out the door today? It is a small thing, but a real thing. The next time you feel the grief rising, the next time the silence feels too heavy, do not try to run from it. Stop. Take a breath. Look at the mirror of your own heart and remember that you are not looking at a void. You are looking at a space that has been filled by the love of a son who is now with the Lord. Say his name. Say the name of Jesus. Let those two names be the melody that carries you through the day. You are a family of four—held in hands that will never let you go. You are not walking toward an end; you are walking toward a reunion. And he is waiting for you in the light, where the mirror is gone, where the tears are wiped away, and where the only thing that remains is the love that you shared, and the love that God has for you, now and forever. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may the light of His face shine upon you and bring you peace. Go in the love of Christ.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Benjamin and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the radiant light of Christ's peace.
For all who are grieving, that the Lord may console them with His presence and fill their hearts with the hope of a glorious reunion.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:
Strive eagerly for the greatest spiritual gifts.

But I shall show you a still more excellent way.

If I speak in human and angelic tongues
but do not have love,
I am a resounding gong or a clashing cymbal.
And if I have the gift of prophecy
and comprehend all mysteries and all knowledge;
if I have all faith so as to move mountains,
but do not have love, I am nothing.
If I give away everything I own,
and if I hand my body over so that I may boast
but do not have love, I gain nothing.

Love is patient, love is kind.
It is not jealous, love is not pompous,
it is not inflated, it is not rude,
it does not seek its own interests,
it is not quick-tempered, it does not brood over injury,
it does not rejoice over wrongdoing
but rejoices with the truth.
It bears all things, believes all things,
hopes all things, endures all things.

Love never fails.
If there are prophecies, they will be brought to nothing;
if tongues, they will cease;
if knowledge, it will be brought to nothing.
For we know partially and we prophesy partially,
but when the perfect comes, the partial will pass away.
When I was a child, I used to talk as a child,
think as a child, reason as a child;
when I became a man, I put aside childish things.
At present we see indistinctly, as in a mirror,
but then face to face.
At present I know partially;
then I shall know fully, as I am fully known.
So faith, hope, love remain, these three;
but the greatest of these is love.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (12) Blessed the people the Lord has chosen to be his own.
Give thanks to the LORD on the harp;
with the ten stringed lyre chant his praises.
Sing to him a new song;
pluck the strings skillfully, with shouts of gladness.
R. Blessed the people the Lord has chosen to be his own.
For upright is the word of the LORD,
and all his works are trustworthy.
He loves justice and right;
of the kindness of the LORD the earth is full.
R. Blessed the people the Lord has chosen to be his own.
Blessed the nation whose God is the LORD,
the people he has chosen for his own inheritance.
May your kindness, O LORD, be upon us
who have put our hope in you.
R. Blessed the people the Lord has chosen to be his own.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus said to the crowds:
“To what shall I compare the people of this generation?
What are they like?
They are like children who sit in the marketplace and call to one another,

‘We played the flute for you, but you did not dance.
We sang a dirge, but you did not weep.’

For John the Baptist came neither eating food nor drinking wine,
and you said, ‘He is possessed by a demon.’
The Son of Man came eating and drinking and you said,
‘Look, he is a glutton and a drunkard,
a friend of tax collectors and sinners.’
But wisdom is vindicated by all her children.”

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben, Trustin visited you today and left you a few airplane cards—we're putting them in your room for you. Please pray for Trustin and his family to stay healthy and strong. Be a guardian angel to Trustin and Ryan as they go through school, and help guide their steps through every year to come.

Ben ơi, Làm cả ngày tới tối, đến lúc chuẩn bị đi ngủ thì nằm một lúc lại nhớ Ben, nhớ mấy chuyện hai anh em từng nói với nhau. Nghĩ tới em, anh thấy buồn nhiều lắm. Ben hãy luôn theo dõi và cầu nguyện cho ba mẹ và Ryan nhé, nước mắt chảy ngược nó khủng khiếp hơn chảy xuôi đó Ben.

Ben ơi, ba nhớ con nhiều quá.

Mommy cũng vậy. Hơn hai tháng rồi mà ba má vẫn khóc mỗi ngày.

Con giúp ba má vượt qua nha, để lo cho em
